newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea '96 trade deficit seen at $20 bln - minister.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea '96 trade deficit seen at $20 bln - minister.

text.p: South Korea's Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy Park Jae-yoon said on Tuesday the nation was expected to post a customs-cleared trade deficit of $20 billion this year against $10.1 billion last year.

"The Korean economy has been having a difficult year," Park told members of American Chamber of Commerce in Seoul. "Our biggest concern is the ballooning trade deficit, which is likely to reach $20 billion for the year as a whole."
The shortfall compares with the trade ministry's official estimate of $19 billion, which was released on Monday.
Ministry officials said the ministry's official forecast for 1996 trade deficit still stood at $19 billion. "Minister Park was probably giving a rough figure," one official said.
Park said the large trade shortfall was due mainly to the fall in the world price of semiconductor chips, the weaker yen and the rapid growth of imports.
Park said South Korea's trade deficit with the United States, Seoul's largest trading partner, would reach $10 billion this year against $6.2 billion in 1995.
Trade deficit in the first 11 months of this year totalled $18.64 billion, up from a $10.01 billion shortfall a year ago.
